newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladeshi bank liquidity improves, says minister.
newsitem.headline: Bangladeshi bank liquidity improves, says minister.

text.p: DHAKA, Aug 5 (Reatur) - Bangladesh's Finance Minister S.A.M.S. Kibria said on Tuesday that the banking sector was overcoming a liquidity crisis by recovering overdue loans.
"According to the central bank some 35 billion taka has been recovered in overdue loans from defaulters," Kibria told a meeting of senior bankers and leading entrepreneurs.
Kibria said the liquidity position of the commercial banks had greatly improved following the loan recovery in just seven months. "It proves the bank-customer relation is very good," he said.
But he said the commercial banks which mobilise funds from savings and term deposits could only offer short term lending.
The total amount of defaulted loan now dropped to 115 billion taka from 150 billion, central bank officials said.
"It's not true that the banking sector is in liquidity crisis now. The bank has sufficient fund for short-term lending," he said.
Kibria said there was sufficient fund with the banks as the interbank call money rate was being traded below the bank rate of 7.5 percent.
"We are struggling for mobilising resources for the long term credit for the large and medium scale industries," he said.
But he said commercial banks together might extend syndicated lending to large industrial projects to minimise risk.

Kibria said foreign banks in Bangladesh were considering forming a consortium for financing big industrial projects. "I had a meeting with all the chief executives of the foreign banks on Monday about the possibilities of forming such consortium," he said.

He said the government had decided to issue bonds to raise a 10 billion taka fund for financing private sector industries over the next year. "This aims to replace industrial lending by commercial banks," he said.
The central bank will start selling the bond later this month.
